_doc: Watch prerequisites. Back-end only - this file is never rendered as a page.
A RUN is an ordered list of STEPS. A row is offerable by Tonight, Up Next
and the random pick if it is in no run, or if every step before its own has
at least one ticked row. Steps, not rows, because one work can sit on
several lists and ticking any copy ticks them all through sync.
A step is written either as a Wikidata id - which expands to EVERY list
carrying that work, so a run defined once applies catalogue-wide - or as
'slug|row-id' for a list that carries no ids. build.py fails loudly on a
step that resolves to nothing, so a typo can never silently do nothing.
SCOPE (Nathan, 2026-08-26). Two rules, and both are about restraint:
1. Direct continuation only, never a shared universe. Fantastic Four (2005)
IS a prerequisite for Rise of the Silver Surfer. It is NOT one for The
Avengers. A run is the smallest set that genuinely confuses out of order.
2. Only where it bites. An ordered list whose rows appear nowhere else
already gets this free - the engine offers it its first unticked row and
nothing else - so Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood needs no entry, and
nor does any series living alone in its own ordered list. A run earns a
place here only when the list is UNORDERED, or the sequence spans lists.

runs._why: CROSS-LIST. Alien 3 is on Fincher's filmography, which has just
runs._why2: become unordered, but the two films before it are not on it at
runs._why3: all. This is the case Nathan asked to be checked for on every
runs._why4: new list: the prerequisite lives somewhere else entirely.
runs.name: Alien

runs._why: CROSS-LIST. Blade Runner 2049 is on Villeneuve; the 1982 film is
runs._why2: on four other lists and none of his.
runs.name: Blade Runner

runs._why: Bond is 27 largely standalone films, but the Craig era is one
runs._why2: continuous story - Quantum of Solace opens an hour after Casino
runs._why3: Royale ends. The other 22 need nothing and stay free.
runs.name: James Bond (Craig)

runs._why: Sanjuro follows Yojimbo with the same character; the source
runs._why2: calls it a sequel. Kurosawa's other 28 films need nothing.
runs.name: Yojimbo

runs._why: CROSS-LIST. The Color of Money is a sequel to The Hustler, which
runs._why2: is not on Scorsese's filmography at all - it is on best-picture.
runs.name: The Hustler

runs._why: A 13-episode story sitting inside a director's filmography. The
runs._why2: list is not a sequence, but this run inside it very much is, and
runs._why3: unordered it would happily offer The Final Episode first.
runs.name: Paranoia Agent

runs._why: Immersive sims is UNORDERED, so its three direct sequels need
runs._why2: saying. System Shock 2's own article: the story was changed
runs._why3: during production into a sequel to the 1994 game.
runs.name: System Shock

runs._why: "It is the sequel to 2012's Dishonored" - and the second game
runs._why2: opens from where the first one leaves the throne.
runs.name: Dishonored

runs._why: Mankind Divided is set two years after Human Revolution with the
runs._why2: same protagonist. The original Deus Ex needs neither first: both
runs._why3: of these are prequels to it.
runs.name: Deus Ex (Jensen)

_notrun: Deliberately absent, as examples of the scope rules above:
Monsters, Inc. -> Monsters University is a PREQUEL, not a continuation;
the source itself says so, and neither needs the other first.
Lightyear is a film the Toy Story characters watch, not a Toy Story film.
Every Pixar film not listed here - WALL-E, Up, Ratatouille, Coco, Soul -
stands alone and is offerable from the very first visit, which is the whole
point of the list being unordered.
